title: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines
seo_title: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines Worksheet (Geometry, G-SRT.D.11) | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g., surveying problems, resultant forces).
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines: area with ½ab sin C, finding sides and angles, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Law of Sines: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.
key_sub: Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C.
body_html:
How it works

SOH CAH TOA only works in right triangles. For any triangle, side a is opposite ∠A, b opposite ∠B, and c opposite ∠C.

  • Area = ½ab sin C (C is the angle between a and b).
  • Law of Sines: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C. Use it when you know a side and its opposite angle (AAS, ASA, SSA).
  • Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C. Use it for SAS (find a side) or SSS (find an angle).

Round only at the end, and keep your calculator in degree mode.

Example

m∠A = 40°, m∠B = 75°, a = 12. Find b.

b/sin 75° = 12/sin 40°

b = 12 sin 75° ÷ sin 40°

Answer: b ≈ 18.0

Example

a = 8, b = 11, m∠C = 60°. Find c.

c² = 64 + 121 − 2(8)(11)(0.5) = 97

Answer: c ≈ 9.8

Common mistakes

  • Using SOH CAH TOA in a triangle without a right angle.
  • Pairing a side with an angle that is not opposite it.
  • Adding 2ab cos C instead of subtracting it.
  • Forgetting to take the square root at the end of the Law of Cosines.

faq.q: When do you use the Law of Sines?
faq.a: When you know an angle and the side opposite it, plus one more side or angle (AAS, ASA or SSA).

faq.q: When do you use the Law of Cosines?
faq.a: When you know two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS).

faq.q: What is the formula for the area of a triangle using sine?
faq.a: Area = ½ab sin C, where C is the angle between sides a and b.

faq.q: Is the Law of Cosines related to the Pythagorean theorem?
faq.a: Yes. When C is 90°, cos C = 0 and the Law of Cosines becomes c² = a² + b².

sets.title: Find an angle and solve problems

items.q: A triangle has sides a = 11, b = 12 and c = 13. Find the largest angle, m∠C, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
You know two angles and one side of a triangle. Which law should you use?
items.e: With two angles and a side (AAS or ASA), you have a complete side-angle pair: use the Law of Sines. Law of Sines.

items.q: A triangle has sides a = 5, b = 8 and c = 9. Find the largest angle, m∠C, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
Two boats leave the same dock. One travels 13 miles and the other travels 10 miles, and the angle between their paths is 120°. How far apart are they, to the nearest tenth of a mile?
items.e: Law of Cosines: d² = 13² + 10² − 2(13)(10) cos 120°, so d = 20.0 miles.

items.q: Which is the Law of Sines?
items.e: Each side is paired with the sine of its opposite angle. a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.

items.q: You know all three sides of a triangle. Which law finds an angle?
items.e: SSS: rearrange the Law of Cosines to find the cosine of an angle. Law of Cosines.

items.q: Two lookout towers are 103 m apart. A fire is seen at angles of 51° and 67° from the line joining the towers. How far is the fire from the first tower (the one with the 51° angle), to the nearest meter?
items.e: The third angle is 62°. The side from the first tower to the fire is opposite the 67° angle: d = 103 × sin 67° ÷ sin 62° = 107 m.

items.q: Two boats leave the same dock. One travels 9 miles and the other travels 14 miles, and the angle between their paths is 50°. How far apart are they, to the nearest tenth of a mile?
items.e: Law of Cosines: d² = 9² + 14² − 2(9)(14) cos 50°, so d = 10.7 miles.

items.q: A triangle has sides a = 8, b = 11 and c = 14. Find the largest angle, m∠C, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
You know two sides and the angle between them. Which law finds the third side?
items.e: SAS gives no matching side-angle pair, so use the Law of Cosines. Law of Cosines.

items.q: In the area formula ½ab sin C, where is angle C?
items.e: C must be the included angle, the one between the two sides you multiply. Between sides a and b.

items.q: What does the Law of Cosines become when m∠C = 90°?
